_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution to the repository test platform — the JSON RFC 8259 `any` mutation vocabulary and the reference implementation that exercises it. `serde_json` is already linked into this crate under the `oracles` feature (see `../../../../../../../../🧪️oracle/📦️packages/🦀️rust/Cargo.toml`, `dep:serde_json`) but had never been registered as a mutation oracle before, so this subset registers its own oracle id for the `json-rfc8259-mutate` capability rather than reusing any shared entry.

oracles.rationale: The reference RFC 8259 JSON reader/writer of the Rust ecosystem, used as the independent producer for every declared `JsonMutation` kind. RFC 8259 §4 declares object member order insignificant, and this crate's default (non-`preserve_order`) `Map` is a `BTreeMap` that re-sorts keys alphabetically on every parse/serialize round trip — real, deliberate producer freedom the `ordered-json-v1` core profile already exists to absorb (array order significant, key order never). Numbers are compared by parsed value, not lexeme, for the same reason: this subset's own codec preserves the original number lexeme verbatim (arbitrary precision, RFC 8259 §6), while `serde_json` without `arbitrary_precision` stores an integer that fits `u64`/`i64` exactly and anything else as `f64` — a real information-loss boundary beyond IEEE-754 double precision that this fixture's real numbers never cross (verified: no number token in the committed fixture exceeds 3 integer digits), so it costs nothing on the real document and is recorded here rather than silently exercised.

productionDebt.plan: serde_json was already a production dependency before this wave — the workspace-level `serde_json = "1.0.149"` (root Cargo.toml) is pulled in directly by this subset's own `📸️snapshot/🦀️component.rs`, whose `From<serde_json::Value> for JsonValue` / `From<JsonValue> for serde_json::Value` interop conversions (and `JsonSnapshot::to_serde_value`) exist for callers elsewhere in the app that want a `serde_json::Value` view of a decoded document; that file's own header comment scopes its 'no serde_json::Value anywhere in this file' claim to the PARSER/SERIALIZER only, not these conversions. Every one of the several hundred production files this entry now records reaches serde_json transitively through `semio_s_plugin_stdio` (or a shared framework crate) for reasons unrelated to this wave's mutation oracle — registering `json-rfc8259-mutate` did not create this reachability, it only made a pre-existing structural fact visible to the dependency gate for the first time. Retiring the debt means one of two deliberate choices for `📸️snapshot/🦀️component.rs`'s owner: move the `serde_json::Value` interop conversions behind a test-only/optional feature so production no longer links them, or reclassify `serde_json` as an accepted permanent (non-test-only) dependency of `semio_s_plugin_stdio` and drop the `testOnly` framing for this capability. Out of this ticket's scope (fleet brief: register the oracle, do not redesign the subset's existing schema module).
